Compute Match — Email Notifications
Emails are rendered by the backend (backend/infrastructure/driven/email/, templates in templates/*.html, subjects in subjects.json). Most are triggered by Temporal workflow activities calling the backend’s System notification APIs (/api/v1/notification/*, scope notification:send).
Customer emails
Email When Reservation request received Right after you submit Custom request received / in review / matched / unserviceable Each custom-request step Offering introduction An NCP accepted; introduces you to the NCP NCP proposed changes An NCP counteroffered Offering rejected An NCP rejected your request (with remarks) Reservation approved / contracted An NCP confirmed the contract Acceptance / contract expired (customer variant) All offerings expired — one consolidated email Reservation rejected / cancelled Final outcomes

Email When Offering magic link (and grouped variant) A request was routed to your organization Magic link resend Someone requested a new link Offering introduction You accepted Expiry reminder 3 days before acceptance deadline Contract expiry reminder 3 days before contract deadline Offering expired / acceptance expired Deadline passed Offering contracted You won the contract Offering superseded Another NCP contracted the same request Reservation cancelled by customer Customer cancelled Future capacity approved / rejected Admin decision on your upload Provider welcome You were onboarded

Email When Future capacity pending review An upload has future capacity to review Custom request received A customer submitted a custom request In-process requests alert Daily 09:00 UTC digest of In Process offerings nearing deadline Access request submitted / notify admin A partner is waiting for NCP access Salesforce sync failure summary Offtake sync failures (when sync is enabled)
Account emails
User activated, user pending activation, access request approved or rejected.
Magic links in detail
Recipients: users of the NCP organization with role provider_business_user and in group offering-validator. Basic users never receive them.
The backend asks the Keycloak extension endpoint POST /realms/{realm}/clustruffle/create-action-token to mint an action token containing the offering id and a nonce.
When clicked, Keycloak validates the nonce with the backend, logs the user in and redirects with from=magic-link.
Valid 1 hour; resend possible for 7 days after routing.
Magic-link emails use the critical retry policy (10 attempts over about 25 minutes) because they are the only way an NCP learns about a request.
Reliability
Ordinary notifications retry 5 times over about 2.5 minutes.
Permanent failures are absorbed (and counted in metric clustruffle_workflow_activity_abandoned) so a workflow replay never re-sends email to users.
